relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-master-password
relations.evidence: By default the Secret Management feature is disabled. To enable the feature, you must first set the master password.

notable_absence.finding: This command's authorization model is explicitly NOT RBAC: it is gated by OS-level group membership ('the user running the command must be a member of the couchbase group (or be root)'), not by any role: or privilege: concept from Couchbase Server's 56-role catalogue. No role name, internal or display, appears anywhere on the page. In a batch this dense with RBAC role citations elsewhere (user-manage.md's ROLES section), the total absence of any RBAC framing here - for a command that unlocks Secret Management's decryption key - is worth flagging: the authorization boundary for the single most sensitive startup operation on a node is an OS group, sitting entirely outside the RBAC vocabulary the rest of this round's registry excerpt is built around. No promoted concept exists yet for 'member of the couchbase OS group', so no relation is asserted for it here rather than fabricating one.

cross_component_finding: The ENVIRONMENT AND CONFIGURATION VARIABLES section (CB_CLIENT_CERT etc.) is copy-pasted verbatim from sibling subcommand pages, including 'See the CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION section for more information' - but master-password.md has no CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION section of its own (unlike setting-master-password.md, which documents the exact same variables AND has the section). This is the same dangling self-reference already flagged on couchbase-cli.json's own extraction record, now confirmed on a second, unrelated subcommand page - suggesting the CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION boilerplate block is pasted onto every ENVIRONMENT AND CONFIGURATION VARIABLES section regardless of whether that specific page defines the section it points to. Consistent with this round's lighter-TW-review hypothesis for cli/.
cross_product_finding: n/a - no Capella/Mobile/SDK content on this page; Secret Management / master-password is a Server-only, on-node concept with no stated Capella equivalent (Capella manages encryption keys at the management-plane level, never via a node-local master password).
